title: Ballad
rule: Each panel carries one rhymed couplet; the page is a ballad of eight couplets.
declares: lines set to rhyme inside the couplets
made: eight panels printed as HANDMADE stencils in flat dyes (the page 08 stencil-dye method: one cut stencil per colour with paper ties, fixed misregistration, mottled dye pooling at the edges) from the b1m2 cut model, on the LoC 1934 sheet
the ANRC 1922 key cutout used as a stencil in ochre, hanging on its drawn hook on the inside of the open cupboard leaf, with a SERVICE tag slip
eight rhymed couplets (ours) in the shared pen hand on pale paper strips across the top of each panel; each couplet's two rhyme words lettered in madder
the memo slip, TICKET OFFICE window lettering and SERVICE cards in the pen hand; hand-ruled borders; folio '22 / Ballad'
couplets: His memo said, as plain could be:
So up he got from desk and chair
to fetch the key from cupboard there.
A lady tapped the glass - a chime:
'Pardon me - have you the right time?'
He looked up at the wall, took stock:
and left the window, left the place.
He reached the cupboard, swung it wide:
the brass key hung, tagged SERVICE, inside.
He stood before the cupboard door:
'Well, here I am... and what for?'
The brass key on its hook would stay;
the SERVICE door stayed shut that day.

events.E5: couplet 7: 'Well, here I am... and what for?' (whole second line); couplet 8: the key stays, the door stays shut

substitutions: none: the four lines are kept word for word and set inside the couplets (declared: lines set to rhyme inside the couplets); the em dash is lettered as the pen hand's dash
beat: the ballad grows panel by panel; the last panel is printed dye by dye (wall wash, then ochre and verdigris, then indigo, madder, skin and umber) and its couplet is pasted on last
